one_liner: GitHub is a web-based developer platform providing REST APIs and webhooks for version control, repository management, and workflow automation.

auth.notes: Personal access tokens, GitHub App installation/user tokens sent as Bearer; OAuth 2.0 for GitHub/OAuth apps (web and device flows); JWT for app-to-server authentication. All tokens sent via Authorization header.

evidence.snippet: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN
you can use Authorization: Bearer or Authorization: token to pass a token
if you are passing a JSON web token (JWT), you must use Authorization: Bearer

access.notes: Any developer can sign up for a GitHub account and immediately create personal access tokens or register OAuth/GitHub Apps with no cost, payment requirement, or vendor approval documented.

evidence.snippet: If you want to use the GitHub REST API for personal use, you can create a personal access token
Sign in to [GitHub](https://github.com/) with the account that should own the app. To keep the app with a team, register it under an organization

api_surface.rate_limit_note: Authenticated requests have higher rate limits than unauthenticated requests; rate limit documentation available.

evidence.snippet: The GitHub REST API is fully described in an OpenAPI compliant document.
Create integrations, retrieve data, and automate your workflows with the GitHub REST API.
Webhooks provide a way for notifications to be delivered to an external web server whenever certain events occur on GitHub
you can make more requests per hour when you are authenticated

buildability.rationale: Self-serve free credentials, fully documented REST API with OpenAPI spec, webhooks support, and broad resource coverage enable immediate toolkit development.
